text:
aj: Quick question about /v1/embeddings — how should the endpoint handle non-string inputs, charset differences, and batch padding/truncation? e.g., bytes/base64, numeric arrays, and mixed types in one batch.

maria: Right now the API accepts only utf-8 strings. We're seeing requests that upstream clients send as base64 or raw bytes for images->text pipelines, and a few customers want stable behavior when mixing languages with different encodings.

ben: For compatibility I'd rather we keep default behavior identical (strings only). If we add different input types we should: require a new explicit param (content_type) and keep old path unchanged. That avoids accidental regressions.

smita: Agreed. Proposal: content_type values: "text" (default), "bytes" (base64 payload), "numbers" (array of ints/floats), "mixed" (array containing multiple types). Server validates and returns 400 for mixed batches unless opt-in header is set.

aj: Two follow-ups: 1) truncation semantics — should we truncate each item independently (per-string truncation) or truncate across the whole batch to meet token limit? 2) output shape — for mixed inputs do we still return one vector per input in the same order, and how do we represent null/invalid items?

maria: For latency and predictability we should do per-item truncation. Global truncation introduces weirdness where a short item could be dropped because a previous item consumed budget. Per-item makes QA and determinism easier.

ben: +1 per-item truncation. Also return an explicit "warnings" array with indices of items that were truncated, and include how they were truncated (bytes->utf8-decoded, trimmed by char count/token heuristic). Example minimal response: 

```json
{ "data": [ {"embedding": [0.001, ...], "index": 0}, {"embedding": [0.01, ...], "index": 1} ], "warnings": [ {"index": 1, "reason": "truncated", "orig_length": 12000, "truncated_to": 8192} ] }
```

smita: For non-string types: if content_type=="bytes" we decode base64 and then attempt utf-8. If decoding fails, return code 422 unless client sets "allow_binary": true which will route to a different transform path (embed raw bytes via a specialized encoder). For "numbers" we treat each numeric array as precomputed token ids or feature vectors — we should probably mark that as "experimental" and not enable by default.

aj: Sounds reasonable. One more: ordering guarantees. If clients send a map like {"id": X, "input": ...}, we must preserve response order matching request order. We also should return the IDs back.

maria: Yes — contract: response.data is ordered to match request order. If request items had an "id" field we echo it back in each data entry. That makes client-side reordering unnecessary.

ben: Backcompat note: default API behavior stays unchanged (strings-only, same truncation rules). New params: content_type, allow_binary (bool), warnings level. Add these to OpenAPI and mention in changelog that mixed/more types are opt-in.

aj: Can someone draft the OpenAPI diff and a short changelog blurb? I'll need to ping customers that requested bytes support.

maria: I'll open a PR with schema changes and example responses. Will include a migration guide: how to opt-in, how to handle warnings array, and example code for clients that previously relied on implicit utf-8 decoding.

smita: PR note: add unit tests for: base64->utf8 success, base64->utf8 failure with allow_binary=false, allow_binary=true path, numeric arrays rejection vs opt-in, and truncated indices reported correctly.

aj: Also pinging @ben for code review on the runtime changes — there's a small kernel change to accept pre-decoded byte buffers. Ben? :point_up:

ben: On it. I'll review the PR today. If changes touch the kernel selection logic we should run the perf benchmark; switching to bytes-to-embedding route may increase batch overhead.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: infra/embeddings-schema-update -> staging at 2026-04-02T02:00:00Z :rocket:

aj: Thanks. Last thing: can we standardize the truncation unit? char count vs token count. My vote is to use token-based truncation with a fallback to chars for unknown encodings, and document limits per-model.

maria: Token-based where we can. For bytes we try utf-8->tokens; if not feasible use byte-length limit. We'll include clear examples in the doc.

aj: Great — I'll collate these notes into the RFC and link the PR. tagging this thread as resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
